extracted.intended_audience: journalism scholars, media researchers, journalism students, and practitioners interested in how news is selected and why
extracted.subtask_description: Analysis of how journalists and newsroom structures decide which national stories become news, emphasizing values, professional standards, and external pressures. Draws on long-term ethnographic observation of major TV and magazine newsrooms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Values shaping journalists' judgments
rubrics_metrics.description: Gans was interested in the values ... that shaped journalists' judgments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on ten years of observing and talking to journalists in major newsrooms; the book treats journalists' personal and professional values as central determinants of what is chosen as national news. Examples discussed include coverage decisions around major headline events (War on Poverty, Vietnam War and protests, urban disorders, assassinations, Watergate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Gans studied the professional standards that shaped journalists' judgments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book examines newsroom norms, routines, and professional criteria journalists use when evaluating stories. It treats these standards as part of why certain events are elevated to national news and discusses how those standards persisted even as media changed.

rubrics_metrics.name: External pressures influencing news choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Gans was interested in the ... external pressures that shaped journalists' judgments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considers pressures from political, social, institutional, and audience factors that constrain or direct newsroom choices. The text situates selection decisions in historical contexts (e.g., major national crises) to show how pressures affected coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational structures' role in news judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: The book suggests that the basics of news judgment and the structures of news organizations have changed little.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues that organizational hierarchies, routines, and institutional roles within TV and magazine newsrooms materially shape which stories are selected; useful for evaluating how structural factors, not just individual reporters, produce news agendas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for selecting national news stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on the journalists who choose the national news stories that inform America about itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit rubric: selection is evaluated by how a story serves the national audience's understanding (newsworthiness for the nation), with historical examples illustrating what editors deemed important. The book provides ethnographic evidence of the practical criteria used in major newsrooms.
